item.title: Four wheels, nine doors, Full of defilement, tied by greed — Mired in mud, O great hero, What will be the future state Of such…
item.description:
Four wheels, nine doors,
Full of defilement, tied by greed —
Mired in mud,
O great hero,
What will be the future state
Of such a human birth?

(The Blessed One):
Having cut off delight and bondage,
Sensual desire and evil,
Having destroyed the root of craving —
Such will be his future state.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.28

item.title: “I do not see any other sound, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a man as the sound of a woman. The…
item.description:
“I do not see any other sound, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a man as the sound of a woman. The sound of a woman, monks, obsesses and occupies the mind of a man.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.2

item.title: “And how, monks, is a monk ‘washed clean’? He has washed away evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful…
item.description:
“And how, monks, is a monk ‘washed clean’? He has washed away evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is ‘washed clean.’”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 39 – Mahāhatthipadopamasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, if that monk, while examining the peril in those thoughts, still has evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion arising, then that…
item.description:
“Monks, if that monk, while examining the peril in those thoughts, still has evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion arising, then that monk should not attend to, not give attention to those thoughts. By not attending to, not giving attention to those thoughts, those evil, unwholesome thoughts are abandoned and subside. With their abandonment, the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated. Monks, just as a person with eyes, not wanting to see forms within his range, would close his eyes or look away; so too, monks, that monk, by not attending … the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 20 – Vitakkasaṇṭhānasutta

item.title: “Monk, whoever thinks about form is bound by Māra. Whoever does not think about form is freed from the Evil One. Whoever thinks about feeling…
item.description:
“Monk, whoever thinks about form is bound by Māra. Whoever does not think about form is freed from the Evil One. Whoever thinks about feeling … perception … formations … consciousness is bound by Māra. Whoever does not think about consciousness is freed from the Evil One. This brief saying of mine, monk, should be understood in detail.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.64

item.title: Standing to one side, the deity Sudatta recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One: As if struck by a sword, As if…
item.description:
Standing to one side, the deity Sudatta recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
As if struck by a sword,
As if fire blazed on the head —
A mindful monk should go forth,
Abandoning lust for sensual pleasures.

(The Blessed One):
As if struck by a sword,
As if fire blazed on the head —
A mindful monk should go forth,
Abandoning identity view.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.16
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Furthermore, Sāriputta, a monk should reflect: ‘Have I abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure?’ Sāriputta, if a monk, on reflection, knows: ‘I have not…
item.description:
“Furthermore, Sāriputta, a monk should reflect: ‘Have I abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure?’ Sāriputta, if a monk, on reflection, knows: ‘I have not yet abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure,’ then he should strive to abandon them. But if, on reflection, he knows: ‘I have abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure,’ then he should dwell with joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 151 – Piṇḍapātapārisuddhisutta

item.title: - What closes in the world? Upon what does the world stand? What hangs up the world? What envelops the world? - Death closes in…
item.description:
- What closes in the world?
Upon what does the world stand?
What hangs up the world?
What envelops the world?
- Death closes in the world,
Upon suffering the world stands,
Craving hangs up the world,
Aging envelops the world.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.68

item.title: “Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple has conscience (hiri): he is ashamed of bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, ashamed of evil, unwholesome states. He has…
item.description:
“Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple has conscience (hiri): he is ashamed of bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, ashamed of evil, unwholesome states. He has fear of wrongdoing (ottappa): he fears bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, fears evil, unwholesome states.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 53 – Sekhasutta

item.title: “Monks, there are these three fires. What three? The fire of greed, the fire of hatred, the fire of delusion. These, monks, are the three…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these three fires. What three? The fire of greed, the fire of hatred, the fire of delusion. These, monks, are the three fires.

The fire of greed burns up people
Who are intoxicated by sensual pleasures.
The fire of hatred burns up
Those who are hateful,
Who kill living beings.

The fire of delusion burns up
Those who are confused,
Not trained in the noble Dhamma.
Not understanding these fires,
People delight in personal existence.

They increase hell,
The realm of animals,
The domain of hungry ghosts,
And also the asuras —
They are not freed
From Māra’s bondage.”

From: Itivuttaka 93
